transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I came in because I just feel... flat inside. Even when my children sit with me, or when the sun is out on my garden, I can’t seem to feel glad or comforted by it. It’s like that part of me has just shut off.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, spending time with family, or going outside?

Yes… I suppose I have. Even when my children come sit with me, or I go out and see the sun on my garden, I don’t really feel anything from it. I used to feel comforted by things like that, but now I just feel flat inside, like that glad feeling has shut off.
Have you been feeling tired or have you noticed a lack of energy most days?
I don’t really know. I mean, I’m 81, so I do get tired, but I haven’t been paying close attention to whether it’s most days or more than usual.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Yes. I used to be able to plan meals and keep my calendar straight, but lately I just… I stare at a grocery list or the senior center schedule and my mind goes blank. I can’t seem to decide even simple things, so my daughter has been helping me with them.
Have you been feeling like you’re a burden to others or that you’re not worth much lately?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been thinking of it in those words… like being worthless. I do worry about needing more help, but I can’t say I’ve noticed feeling that I’m not worth much.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately? Like eating more or less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been weighing myself or keeping track. I don’t think I’ve noticed a big change in my appetite, but I couldn’t say for certain.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?
I don’t know that I’d call it depressed most of the day every day. I’ve felt upset and not like myself, but I’m not sure it’s the same as being down nearly all day.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself moving slower, and I can’t say I’ve been especially restless either. I just haven’t paid much attention to that.
Looking back, would you say that most days have felt down or sad to you, and that this has been happening for several weeks or longer?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had some hard days and I haven’t felt like myself, but I don’t know that I’d say most days have been down or sad for several weeks.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that most days you felt down or depressed most of the day?
I’m still not sure I’d say depressed most of the day. I’ve had some rough days, but I can’t really say it was most days, all day like that.
Looking back, would you say that there have been at least two weeks in a row where you felt down or sad most days, even if it wasn’t all day every day?
I don’t really know. I’ve felt off and sad at times, but I can’t clearly say there was a full two weeks in a row where it was most days.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that on most days you felt down, sad, or emotionally flat for most of the day—even if it wasn’t all day?

Yes… I think so. It’s more like I feel flat inside. Even when my children come sit with me, or the sun is out on my garden, I just don’t feel the comfort or gladness I used to. It’s like that part of me has shut off.
Have you found that things that used to bring you pleasure, like seeing your children or enjoying your garden, no longer feel enjoyable or rewarding to you?

Yes. That’s why I came in, really. Even when my children sit with me, or the sun is on my garden, I just feel flat inside. It’s like the part of me that could feel glad or comforted has just shut off.
Would you say that during the past two weeks, there have been several days where you felt down, sad, or emotionally flat for most of the day, even if not all the time?

Yes… several days, yes. It’s that flat feeling I keep talking about. Even when my children are with me, or I’m looking out at the sun on my garden, I don’t feel the gladness or comfort I used to. It feels like that part of me has just shut off.
Would you say that for at least two weeks in a row, you felt down, sad, or emotionally flat for most of the day, on most days—even if not all the time?
Yes… it’s been about two weeks now. Ever since my husband collapsed and the paramedics were working on him in our kitchen, I’ve been like this most days.

inference_history.note: The patient reports feeling flat and unable to feel glad or comforted, suggesting anhedonia. This symptom is common to several disorders including major depressive disorder (F32.1, F32.2, F33.1, F33.2), persistent depressive disorder (F34.1), adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21), and personality disorder (F60.5), among others.
